definitions.explanation: A person who has been captured and held, especially an enemy taken in battle. A formal, literary word now found mainly in writing, history, and translation.

examples.japanese: {虜囚|りょしゅう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
⟦{敵|てき}→敵：03546_teki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{虜囚|りょしゅう}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{扱|あつか}われた→扱う：01862_atsukau⟧。
examples.english: He was treated as a captive of the enemy.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長|なが}い→長い：00491_nagai⟧{虜囚|りょしゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、ようやく⟦{解放|かいほう}→解放：00135_kaihou⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He was finally freed after a long captivity.

notes:
A formal, somewhat literary term. In everyday speech ⟦{捕虜|ほりょ}→捕虜：20662_horyo⟧ is far more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {虜囚|りょしゅう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to become a captive
- {虜囚|りょしゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧: the status of a captive
- {虜囚|りょしゅう}⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧: life in captivity

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{捕虜|ほりょ}→捕虜：20662_horyo⟧: prisoner of war — the ordinary, neutral word
- ⟦{人質|ひとじち}→人質：09678_hitojichi⟧: hostage — held to force concessions, not captured in battle
